questions.stem: In the context of the structure of the Earth, what is the 'Moho' (Mohorovičić discontinuity)?

options.option_text: The boundary separating the Earth's crust from the underlying mantle
The boundary separating the inner core from the outer core
The deepest trench in the Pacific Ocean
The boundary between the troposphere and stratosphere

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Discovered by Croatian seismologist Andrija Mohorovičić in 1909, the Moho is the boundary between the Earth's crust (the brittle outer shell) and the much denser, hotter mantle below. Seismologists mapped it because seismic waves suddenly accelerate when they cross this boundary, indicating a sharp change in rock density.
DECOY BUSTING: The boundary between the outer core and inner core is the Lehmann discontinuity. The boundary between the mantle and outer core is the Gutenberg discontinuity. The boundary between troposphere and stratosphere is the tropopause.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Moho is much deeper under the continents (about 30-50 km down) than it is under the oceans (only 5-10 km down) because oceanic crust is much thinner.

questions.stem: Which of the following rocks is an example of an Igneous rock?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava. Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock formed from the rapid cooling of lava exposed at or very near the surface of the Earth. (The oceanic crust is mostly basalt).
DECOY BUSTING: Sandstone is a Sedimentary rock (formed from compressed sand). Marble is a Metamorphic rock (formed when limestone is subjected to intense heat and pressure). Slate is a Metamorphic rock (formed from shale).
EXAM INSIGHT: Granite is another very famous igneous rock, but it is 'intrusive'—it cools slowly deep underground, allowing large, visible crystals to form.
